Conclusion

Classification: only consequence-distinct ordered-identity support is established.

The comparison is valid on the stated design, not an invalid comparison. It establishes the host-feasibility prerequisite strongly. It does not establish prospective same-information native allocation or bounded-utility headroom over a competent GAE comparator.

Question	Judgment
Can exactly three persistent agents support balanced, consequence-distinct ordered waiter identities?	Yes, in this host.
Is there decision-relevant oracle headroom over competent same-information GAE?	No.
Is the tiny positive probability difference meaningful headroom?	No; statistically resolved but scientifically negligible.
Does the source-localized panel validate the waiter consequence path?	Yes for host causality; no positive algorithmic advantage exists to localize.
Does this justify a relay experiment?	No.

This is a sharper result than “nothing worked.” The observation closes one important loophole in B1—nominal waiter identity can now genuinely alter consequence—but it simultaneously shows that a competent ordinary estimator already captures that relation.

Relation to the frozen B1 object

B1 was explicitly an association-relay experiment: the later joiner request was the source action, the true older waiter’s changed execution and downstream utility were the target effect, and the association-bearing kappa packet was attached to the later joiner’s record while the waiter retained ordinary GAE. Its four-world construction separated the joiner effect, waiter marginal, generic waiter marginal, and ordered interaction.

B1 also prospectively required more than expressibility. Association-specific support required native selectivity and native utility improvements over both GAE and the binding cut, utility means of at least 0.05, positive native-minus-yoked interactions, actual common-uniform request changes, and matched token, work, clock, and optimizer controls. Its update was a single full-batch normalized-gradient step with a common KL-derived trust radius.

The retained result did not satisfy those criteria: D_IG_N, D_IG_Y, and Psi_G were all exactly zero, and the result marked both native utility superiority and native-minus-yoked interactions as false. The direction consequently records that expressibility/selectivity passed while allocation and utility improvement were zero.

The new host therefore answers a legitimate post-B1 question: perhaps B1 saturated because the nominal physical waiter identity did not actually change consequence once generic type and lag were fixed. The answer is now:

A three-agent host can remove that identity-consequence deficiency, but removing it does not create oracle-versus-GAE value headroom.

Prerequisite 1: ordered identity support is established

The causal-support evidence is unusually clean.

For each joiner, the two eligible waiters differ in physical compatibility while cue sign, lag, propensity, readiness, budget, and clock remain matched. Each persistent identity is favorable for one joiner and unfavorable for another, eliminating waiter-ID main effects. The exact zero waiter and joiner marginals and zero single-deployment effects further rule out interpreting the result as “some agents are simply better” or “deployment is generically useful.”

The +0.4/-0.4 favorable/unfavorable Delta and kappa, together with a 0.8 favorable-minus-unfavorable natural effect and interaction contrast, establish that consequence is carried by the ordered joiner–waiter relation. The source-localized severing result then identifies the mechanism: when immediate deployment of the true waiter is removed, all of those contrasts collapse to zero.

There is one important wording restriction. This is not evidence that a nominal identity has an intrinsic causal property. Compatibility is generated by deployed output/input port occupancy. The supported object is therefore:

a fixed-population, pair-indexed physical compatibility relation represented by ordered identities, not identity independent of physical state.

That is nevertheless sufficient for the requested host-feasibility prerequisite. It demonstrates balanced, consequence-distinct eligible waiter identities within this exact three-agent cycle.

Prerequisite 2: native headroom over competent GAE fails

The decisive evidence is not the sampled token count. It is the noiseless competence panel:

every GAE gradient sign matched the pair-Q oracle;

gradient cosine was effectively one;

noiseless favorable-allocation probability differed by exactly zero;

the maximum Bellman residual was at machine precision.

These facts show that the ordered pair and its expected consequence are already represented in ordinary GAE’s state/value problem. At population level, the pair-Q oracle supplies no different decision direction. It principally replaces sampled-return noise with a conditional expectation.

The sampled GAE result reinforces competence: its favorable-token fraction was 0.56337, with a root interval wholly above chance. That performance is not optimal, but the remaining task headroom is shared headroom under the one-step trust constraint. It is not headroom that the oracle captures and GAE misses.

The positive probability contrast is not decision-relevant

The oracle-minus-GAE probability difference was

2.2238206×10
−5
,

or approximately 0.00222 percentage points.

That is roughly 4,497 times smaller than an absolute 0.10 allocation-fraction margin. At 96 evaluator tokens per root, it corresponds to only:

approximately 0.00213 expected additional favorable tokens per root;

approximately 0.0256 expected additional tokens over all 12 roots.

Thus exact zero common-uniform allocation differences are the expected realization of an effect this small. Increasing token count could eventually reveal an occasional extra token, but the normalized allocation difference would still converge to approximately 0.000022, not to 0.10. More tokens would estimate a negligible effect more precisely; they would not manufacture prospective headroom.

The positive confidence interval should therefore not be dismissed as floating-point error. It is likely a real, systematic finite-batch variance-reduction effect. But statistical resolvability of an internal policy probability is not the registered scientific endpoint. The policy difference failed to cross any actual allocation boundary and produced exactly zero bounded-utility difference at every root.

Common-uniform discretization is doing its intended job

Common uniforms are not an unfair obstacle here. They test whether a policy-probability change reaches actual decisions while reducing treatment-comparison noise. A threshold-scale 0.10 probability or allocation effect would imply roughly 9.6 changed choices per 96-token root under a reasonably distributed interior policy. The observed effect implies two-thousandths of one change per root.

Consequently, the evaluator is not plausibly hiding a near-threshold treatment effect. It is revealing that the surrogate probability difference does not reach the finite decision surface.

Request and update geometry do not rescue the result

The common one-step full-batch trust geometry intentionally makes update direction, rather than unconstrained gradient magnitude, the comparison. B1 likewise used arm-local advantage normalization followed by a common normalized displacement and KL-frozen trust radius.

That geometry can suppress a mechanism whose only distinction is gradient scale. But changing it now would change the scientific object from association-specific credit to optimizer calibration, step-size accumulation, or multi-update learning. Here the noiseless update directions are already collinear. There is no evidence that the special target points toward a better pair allocation that GAE fails to identify.

A claim that many updates might accumulate the 2.2×10⁻⁵ difference is also outside this single-update object. More importantly, accumulation of a finite-sample denoising advantage would still require comparison against a generic expected-Q or Rao–Blackwellized control before it could be called association-specific delayed credit.

The exact-value GAE comparator is appropriately strong

The exact pair-aware finite-state value does not invalidate the comparison. It makes the conclusion narrower and more credible.

The investment question is whether a specialized association mechanism has value beyond competent ordinary GAE under the same information. An exact value is the cleanest way to prevent critic misspecification from masquerading as a credit-assignment discovery. Because both arms receive the ordered pair and the same six-entry policy head, the comparator is not being denied the relation that the candidate is supposed to exploit.

Weakening the critic would likely create some oracle-minus-GAE gap through one or more of:

critic approximation error;

bootstrapping bias;

finite-data variance;

incomplete value learning;

function-sharing interference.

Such a gap could be useful in a separately defined estimator-robustness project. It would not establish association-specific delayed credit without controls showing that the gain exceeds a generic conditional-Q denoiser with the same information, data, capacity, and computation.

B1’s science card anticipated exactly this confound: a relay label could merely be a denser or lower-variance surrogate for favorable renewal contexts, so improvement over ordinary GAE and matched physical yoking were required before giving it an association interpretation.

On the present numbers, generic expected-Q denoising is a sufficient explanation of the tiny probability advantage. No residual association-specific value has been demonstrated.

Source localization: adequate, but only for the host mechanism

The localized panel is well designed for its stated purpose. Holding pair context, Q table, tapes, head, data, optimizer, and evaluator fixed while severing the waiter transition asks whether downstream effects require the source-to-waiter execution path.

Its two findings should be separated:

Causal-support localization succeeds.
The favorable/unfavorable causal contrasts collapse exactly to zero. That strongly supports the interpretation that the ordered interaction operates through immediate deployment of the true waiter and subsequent bounded route service.

Algorithmic path-specific value does not appear.
Local oracle-minus-GAE utility was approximately −0.0005425, and native-minus-local was approximately +0.0005425; both intervals span zero. The latter is about 92 times smaller than the frozen 0.05 path-specific margin.

Retaining the native Q table after severing makes this a fixed-policy mediation intervention, not a newly solved severed environment. That is appropriate for localization. It would not be appropriate to treat the localized branch as an independently optimized comparator. Nothing in the supplied interpretation requires doing so.

The panel therefore adequately protects the statement:

the host’s ordered-pair consequence runs through the waiter transition.

It does not support:

the oracle has a delayed-waiter-path advantage over GAE.

There is essentially no native advantage to localize.

Host feasibility, relay value, and denoising are different conclusions

The evidence supports the following separation:

Host feasibility: positive. A fixed population of exactly three agents can instantiate balanced, consequence-distinct ordered waiter relations with zero identity marginals and a source-localized physical path.

Ordinary-credit competence: positive. Exact-value, pair-aware GAE recovers the correct pair-Q gradient and exceeds chance.

Generic expected-Q denoising: weakly positive in probability space. The oracle gives a tiny finite-batch probability advantage.

Decision-relevant oracle headroom: negative under the frozen criteria. Actual allocation and bounded utility are exactly equal.

Association-specific delayed credit: untested and unsupported. No relay target or binding comparison was run, and the prerequisite for running one failed.

Relay value: no conclusion beyond “not currently justified.”

This also weakens an association interpretation of B1’s binding-cut contrast. It does not prove that the B1 cut was invalid, but the present host shows that genuine pair consequences do not automatically cause ordinary GAE to fail. The earlier native cut advantage remains compatible with cue/type anti-supervision or another label-assignment effect rather than physical waiter identity.

Investment recommendation
PARK PENDING GENUINELY NEW EVIDENCE

Operationally, the present exactly-three-agent object should be considered closed. Preserve it as a positive causal-support fixture, but do not continue experimental work at the same scope.

A narrower prerequisite-only research line is not justified: the identity-support prerequisite has already been answered cleanly. More host-only work cannot alter relay investment unless it also reveals prospective native headroom.

A generic expected-Q-denoising spin-off is also not presently justified by an allocation gap of zero and a utility gap of zero. Such a spin-off would require an independently motivated estimator-efficiency question and a materially larger prospective effect, not relabeling this tiny probability contrast.

No relay should run.

Material objections that remain

The new implementation was not connector-auditable.
Its result is assessed as the supplied frozen evidence packet. A hidden information leak, value-table construction error, or post-treatment input could change validity, although the reported controls give no indication of one.

The comparator is stronger than a typical learned critic.
This limits external relevance. It does not weaken the bounded null against competent GAE, and replacing it with an inferior critic would answer a different question.

The policy directly receives the ordered pair.
That may make the relation primarily a representation/lookup problem rather than a difficult temporal-association problem. This is part of why exact GAE saturates.

Compatibility is physical occupancy, not irreducible nominal identity.
The result establishes relational identity support only. A policy supplied with explicit port-occupancy features might solve the same problem without persistent identity keys.

Only one update is tested.
Multi-update coadaptation, learned critics, and accumulated estimator variance remain unstudied. They cannot be used to overturn this single-update result.

Source localization holds the learned/update objects fixed.
It is a valid mediation control, but it does not tell us how either learner would adapt if trained in the severed environment.

A statistically nonzero probability effect remains.
This is real counterevidence to literal oracle–GAE equality in sampled finite batches. Its lack of decision and utility translation is why it does not alter the investment decision.

Strongest evidence against my conclusion

The strongest countercase combines three observations:

the oracle probability contrast has a confidence interval wholly above zero;

sampled GAE is only about 0.563 favorable rather than near-perfect;

an exact pair-aware value is more favorable to GAE than realistic learned critics may be.

Together, those facts leave open a different hypothesis: a low-variance pair-Q estimator might improve finite-data learning when the critic must be learned.

They do not establish the current prerequisite because the noiseless gradients coincide, the remaining performance headroom is common to both arms, and the prospective native endpoints are exactly equal. Pursuing the alternative would require a new learned-estimator object with generic denoising controls—not a weakened rerun of this comparison.

Common failure risk for finite-host credit directions

The central shared risk is same-information Q-sufficiency collapse:

Once the entire consequence-bearing relation is represented in the finite state and policy head, a competent ordinary value estimator converts the apparently delayed causal association into ordinary expected action value. A specialized counterfactual label may then improve variance, diagnostics, or interpretability without changing the decision.

Related finite-host risks are expressibility without value, normalized-update collinearity, discrete action aliasing of small probability effects, and false-positive binding cuts that corrupt a generic cue-to-consequence relation rather than isolate identity.

Smallest scientifically distinct reentry discriminator

The smallest defensible reentry is not another sampled run. It is a prospective, exact-enumeration pre-relay certificate on a genuinely new host:

Construct a new fixed three-agent host with balanced ordered-pair support and the same strict information parity.

Before collecting terminal tokens, enumerate the finite state/tape distribution and calculate the post-update policy under:

competent exact-value GAE;

a generic pair-aware conditional-Q or Rao–Blackwellized return estimator;

the proposed oracle prerequisite.

Pass the actual common trust map and evaluator analytically, reporting expected native favorable allocation and normalized bounded utility—not merely gradient cosine or probability selectivity.

Require the existing decision standard: at least 0.10 native allocation and utility gains over competent GAE, with positive predeclared-root lower bounds.

Require a source-localized native-minus-severed effect of at least 0.05.

Stop before any relay if the population updates remain collinear, if the evaluator-level margin fails, or if the oracle advantage is matched by generic expected-Q denoising.

Only after that prerequisite succeeds would a relay comparison become admissible, and that later comparison would still need a generic expected-Q denoiser to distinguish association-specific credit from variance reduction.

Maximum bounded claim

In this one fixed-population, exactly three-agent, finite-horizon, bounded, single-update constructed host, balanced ordered joiner–waiter relations can be made causally consequence-distinct and source-localized, but a prospective pair-Q oracle provides no decision-relevant actual-allocation or bounded-utility improvement over competent exact-value GAE under the frozen update and evaluator.
